reflection.assumptions: The impact of the pandemic and the legacy of Ebola should be understood through how participants describe changes in healthcare, perceptions of risk, institutional responses, and everyday experiences during public health crises. Additionally, the interplay between traditional medicine and modern healthcare practices may be more significant than previously assumed, highlighting the need to consider cultural beliefs in depth. Moreover, the emotional and psychological aspects of healthcare workers' experiences during the pandemic may require further exploration, particularly regarding their coping mechanisms and resilience. I also recognize that the framing of healthcare experiences can differ based on the perspectives of various stakeholders, such as patients, healthcare workers, and policymakers.
reflection.further_consideration: How do the evolving perceptions of patients and healthcare workers regarding COVID-19 reflect broader societal attitudes toward health crises? Additionally, what are the implications of the perceived effectiveness of communication about COVID-19 on healthcare practices and patient behavior? How might the differences in coding across perspectives inform our understanding of the interrelationships between fear, responsibility, and healthcare delivery?

coding_output:
Initial Code: Patient inflow decreases due to fear of COVID-19  
Clues: "But as soon as they sound the bell that there is a confirmed case in Sierra Leone, the patients in-flow dropped drastically. Right? Virtually when you come to the hospital at that time, the hospital was empty. The patients were scared. They were afraid."  
Initial Code: Patients believe hospitals are sources of COVID-19  
Clues: "They think that when they come to the hospital they will catch the virus. That the doctors and nurses make the virus."  
Initial Code: Increased responsibilities for health workers during the pandemic  
Clues: "No. In fact as a matter of fact, it increased. ... Because I’ve to see the covid patients, and also do my normal clinical work. Right? So it doubled up."  
Initial Code: Implementation of triage system to manage patient flow  
Clues: "But now it is instituted by management that all patients should have a triage form where in their vitals will be recorded and also other signs and symptoms will be recorded."  
Initial Code: Reduction of patient beds to prevent crowding  
Clues: "The spacing of the patients’ bed in the ward. Beds were been reduced. Yeh, because covid doesn’t favor crowded places."  
Initial Code: Elective surgeries postponed during the COVID-19 peak  
Clues: "We laid a law at the surgical department that only emergency patients will be operated on. …All elective cases were put on hold."  
Initial Code: Initial panic about COVID-19 subsides over time  
Clues: "But as time passes by, the effect of afraid became drain by people. People start to believe, to assume now that the corona virus is with us."  
Initial Code: Staff trained on COVID-19 protocols  
Clues: "That was a change. For example, for the use of the face masks, it was not compulsory in the hospital. But now it became compulsory as soon as you are at the hospital’s gate."  
Initial Code: Challenges with personal protective equipment (PPE) availability  
Clues: "Because the way and manner in…..how the virus was being, and the lack of IPC gears at that point in time. There were few masks, few of the gowns to be used."  
Initial Code: Management's response to prepare for COVID-19  
Clues: "The hospital management also called several meetings and also puts a lot of things and structures in place. ...By controlling the main gate for the flow of people, encouraging people to wash their hands."  
Initial Code: Changes in patient demographics due to COVID-19  
Clues: "Two districts have outbreak of covid in their theaters. So they had their theaters shut down. So those patients were been referred to the [retracted] government hospital."  
Initial Code: Staff reassignment for COVID-19 response  
Clues: "Those that were assigned to see covid patients, most of them were stopped from seeing none covid patients."  
Initial Code: Staffing shortages increase workload  
Clues: "The more the better, but the less the more difficult work will be. So definitely those that were left in the department will face huge challenge of work."  
Initial Code: Training improves care for COVID-19 patients  
Clues: "Yes there were trainings, especially in the line of covid-19. Were those staffs assigned to the covid-19 had their initial phase of training."  
Initial Code: Training affects work progress  
Clues: "It affected work, Yah. For that day, the load, the work progress will be slow for that day."  
Initial Code: Increased stress related to COVID-19  
Clues: "Everyone was stressed. That was why many people were willing to attend the training. Because you were stressed of catching the virus."  
Initial Code: Fear of infection inhibits patient care  
Clues: "For me, I was afraid. I was scared. Especially when there is no glove, I don’t touch patients."  
Initial Code: Need for personal protective equipment (PPE)  
Clues: "Because you don’t have your proper gears to use."  
Initial Code: Government support for protective measures  
Clues: "Later on the government then intervened and sent those IPCs- gloves, masks, the N95s."  
Initial Code: Decrease in patient flow during the pandemic  
Clues: "Just as I have said, the patients flow decreased. When the outbreak stared, there were minimal patients that we saw at the department."  
Initial Code: Communication about COVID-19 is perceived as adequate  
Clues: "No, no. I don’t think so. [...] But mostly by the news."  
Initial Code: Perception of COVID-19 compared to Ebola  
Clues: "Covid-19 is simple to catch but not as fatal as Ebola."
